text.en: Asha touched a hot pan and pulled her hand away before she even thought. "That is a reflex," said her teacher.

The nervous system controls and coordinates body activities. Its unit is the neuron, made of the cell body, dendrites and an axon. Neurons are sensory, motor or association neurons, and nerve fibres can be myelinated or non-myelinated. An impulse passes along a neuron as an electrical signal and across a synapse with chemicals called neurotransmitters.
The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord. The brain is protected by the skull and bathed in cerebrospinal fluid. A reflex action is a quick automatic response to a stimulus, controlled by the spinal cord through a reflex arc.
The peripheral nervous system has cranial and spinal nerves, and the autonomic nervous system controls involuntary actions like heartbeat through its sympathetic and parasympathetic parts.

problem.en: Name the two parts of the central nervous system.

text.en: The central part commands the body.
It is made of the brain.

prompt.en: A friend says Reflex actions are controlled by the cerebrum. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Reflexes are quick, spinal cord responses.
They do not wait for thinking.
